title: Analysing data to draw conclusions
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Data is only useful when we read it and act on it. By comparing the numbers, we can draw conclusions and make sensible decisions. Quick words: data means facts and numbers collected to help us understand something. conclusions means answers or decisions you make after looking at the facts. stock means the goods a shop keeps ready to sell to customers.
Compare the values in a table or graph to see which is the most and which is the least.

steps: A shop sold 5 red, 8 blue and 3 green shirts.
Compare the numbers: 8 is the biggest.
So blue shirts sold the most.

blocks.prompt: A shop sold 5 red, 8 blue, 3 green shirts. Which colour sold most? ___
blocks.explain: 8 is the largest number, and that is blue.
blocks.rule: Compare the values to find which category is greatest or least.

practiceItems.prompt: the most sold, where red=5, blue=8, green=3

blocks.content: Use what the data shows to make a decision — for example, stock more of what sells best.

blocks.question: If blue shirts sell the most, the shop should stock more:
blocks.explain: Stocking more of the best-seller (blue) is the sensible decision.
blocks.rule: Use the data to make a sensible decision, like stocking more of the best-seller.

practiceItems.prompt: stock more of the ___ selling item (best/worst)

blocks.question: A shop's ice-cream sales were: Monday 10, Tuesday 12, Wednesday 30, Thursday 11. Which day stands out, and what might explain it?
options: Wednesday — 30 is far above the usual 10-12, perhaps a very hot day
Monday, because it is the lowest
blocks.explain: Most days sold around 10 to 12, but Wednesday sold 30 — much higher than the rest. A value far from the others stands out, and a real reason (like a hot day) often explains it. Reading data means spotting what is unusual and asking why.
blocks.rule: Look for values far from the others, then think about why.
blocks.principle: Data analysis is not just reading numbers, but noticing and explaining what is unusual.
canonical_solution: A likely reason: a very hot day boosts ice-cream sales

rubric.look_for: compares each day to the others
identifies Wednesday as far above the rest
offers a sensible reason for the unusual value

misconceptions.coach: The one that STANDS OUT is far from the others — that is Wednesday's 30.
Compare days to spot the unusual one.

blocks.content: Compare the numbers, draw your conclusion, and let the data guide your decision. Let's practise!
